correctness.rationale: A self-contained root-order lemma proves correctness of the maximality predicate; every binary host up to seven is covered by exact length bounds and a 4-template insertion census with all 8 exceptions listed. Two independent executable exhaustive checks agree. The arbitrary-m proof uses exact marker count and the single intervening zero to bound mixed roots by 2; the 2m+1 zeros give maximum root length m. Code is finite corroboration only.

value.rationale: Maximal square subsequences are algorithmically motivated by the January 2026 near-linear maximal algorithm. The sharp first nontrivial mixed-letter case, its complete 8-word orbit census and a family with arbitrarily bad maximal-to-maximum size ratio provide a structural boundary rather than a mere easy normalization or isolated toy count. This motivates separating feasibility-poset maximality from optimum length.
